chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yūnus, from Ibn Miskān, from Ibn Abī Yaʿfūr, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who does not know whether he has prayed two rakʿahs or four. He said: “He recites the tashahhud and gives salām, then stands and prays two rakʿahs and four sajdahs, reciting in them Fātiḥat al-Kitāb. Then he recites the tashahhud and gives salām. If he had in fact prayed four, then these two would be supererogatory; and if he had prayed two, then these two would complete the four. And if he had spoken, then let him perform the two sajdahs of forgetfulness.”

key_terms.أَرْبَعًا: four rakʿahs, referring to the full prayer under doubt
key_terms.إِتْمَامَ الْأَرْبَعَةِ: completion of the four rakʿahs if only two had actually been prayed
key_terms.سَجْدَتَيِ السَّهْوِ: the two prostrations performed for forgetfulness in salat (prayer)
key_terms.فَاتِحَةِ الْكِتَابِ: Sūrat al-Fātiḥah, to be recited in the remedial prayer
key_terms.نَافِلَةً: a supererogatory prayer if the original obligatory prayer was already complete

ai.seo_question: What should a person do in salat if he doubts whether he prayed two rakʿahs or four?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for one who doubts in salat (prayer) whether he has prayed two rakʿahs or four. He should conclude the prayer, then pray two additional rakʿahs with Fātiḥat al-Kitāb; if his original prayer was complete they count as nafilah, and if not they complete the obligation. If he spoke, he must also perform the two sajdahs of forgetfulness.
